reason_for_v1: The preregistered v0 global execution correctly hit its 3000-compile guard after eight complete searches and one partial search. Its implementation also shared compilation cache across search variants/starts, so its zero additional compilation counts for later cached searches cannot be used to compare search overhead. V1 is a new, outcome-aware follow-up that isolates each search in a fresh compiler/cache and charges every candidate compilation to that search. V0 result scope remains unchanged.

search.width_pruned_relocation: compile candidates with vertex-separation width <= current_width + 1 only
search.selection: minimum final live ROBDD nodes, then minimum allocated nodes, then lexicographic order
search.compiler: fresh balanced-pairwise ROBDD manager for every candidate; no compilation cache may be shared across search cells

resource_guard.on_guard: mark cell incomplete; do not call it a local optimum

correctness: Every completed cell's final order must exactly reproduce the predecessor family rank vector. The final selected order is additionally checked by exact full assignment bitset equality when materializing the persistent result artifact.
predeclared_tests: For each family/start, compare width-pruned vs full final live nodes and compiled-candidate count using fresh independent caches.
Call width-only pruning safe on a cell only if it reaches the same final live-node count as full relocation; otherwise record a miss, regardless of average savings.
Report path dependence between natural and reverse-Cuthill-McKee starts; do not call either local endpoint global optimum.
Report search cost separately from one-shot final compilation cost; no hidden amortization across variants.
No result is a CUDD dynamic-sifting benchmark.
